{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Licence, Development and Supply Agreement (Ono / Array)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings — 19 rules tested  
**Status:** Confidential — attorney work product

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial core of the deal (licence scope, payment structure, absence of minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicitation and renewal mechanics) is acceptable and in several places better than our fallback, so we are not redlining it. The exposure is concentrated in five areas: (i) Array gives us **no IP infringement, breach of law, confidentiality or misconduct indemnity** while our indemnity to Array is very broad; (ii) the Agreement contains **no aggregate liability cap at all**, leaving our direct liability unlimited; (iii) **mandatory ICC arbitration seated in Osaka at Array's election**, notwithstanding the New York governing-law clause; (iv) an **exclusive-dealing / non-compete covenant on us of undefined in-term length with an undefined post-termination tail** and no performance-based exit; and (v) **no termination for convenience** until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products.

Three findings could not be completed or verified and require manual attention before we table anything: ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP), the proposed liability cap (LOL-CAP) and termination for convenience (T4C). We should not send the mark-up until those are cleared.

We would also note two structural gaps rather than deviations: there is **no Array-side transition assistance or return of our data** on expiry or termination (the wind-down regime runs one way, against us), and **no insurance covenant** anywhere despite Array's indemnity and recall exposure.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.1–16.3) | No IP infringement, breach of law, confidentiality or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover and no duty to defend; our indemnity in 16.1 is far broader. Fails fallback and preferred. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (verification failed). Manual review required; no conclusion reached. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation *(redline repaired)* | § VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | Exclusive dealing for an undefined redacted in-term period plus post-termination tail, with no exit for Array supply failure. Redline caps at 12 months and adds a self-executing exit tied to Array's Article 9 supply obligations. |
| High | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | General Provisions (18.3; 17.3) | New York law is agreed and untouched; forum fails preferred and fallback — mandatory three-arbitrator ICC arbitration seated in Osaka whenever Array demands. Redline converts to exclusive New York County jurisdiction, preserving temporary injunctive relief elsewhere. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § XIV Effect of Termination | No LDs, penalties or exit fee payable by us. The only LD provision (14.3) runs in our favour and must not be redlined. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § II Grant of License | Affiliates covered without consent or notice; successor transferability under 18.9; perpetual paid-up conversion on expiry (13.1). At or above fallback. Noted only: Third Party sublicensee/distributor appointment needs Array consent. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Needs review** | Indemnification; Recalls (16.5) | No aggregate cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited both ways, failing the fallback 12-month cap. Proposed new 16.7 (mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1m, Excluded Claims uncapped, all Ono payment obligations excluded). Verification failed — placement and the USD 1m floor need confirmation. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | Not confined to the term, not capped at 12 months, no acquisitions carve-out, and an Ono-only post-termination tail of undefined length. Narrowed to fallback rather than deleted to preserve the retained royalty and termination mechanics. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | Term and Termination (13.2) | No at-will exit until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products; notice period redacted and unverifiable against 30/60–90 day thresholds. Proposed 30 days' notice at any time plus pro rata refund of period-allocated prepayments. Verification failed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § VII Payments; Books and Records (7.4; 4.9(a)) | 7.4 is close to position but notice is only "reasonable" and the cost-shifting underpayment threshold is redacted; 4.9(a) gives Array an open-ended facility inspection right with no frequency cap. Target fallback: 15 days' notice, once yearly, cost-shift above 10%. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § IX Product Manufacturing and Supply | No MFN, price-parity or right-to-match obligation on us; the two favourability provisions run in our favour or are neutral. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | Compliant | § IX Product Manufacturing and Supply | Supply framed as our right, not obligation (9.4(a), 9.4(b)); payments are event- or usage-based. Re-test when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are negotiated. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | General Provisions | No no-hire or anti-poaching covenant; the 18.10 / 4.5(b) firewalls do not restrict hiring. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | Term and Termination (13.1; 14.4) | No evergreen mechanic; term self-executes to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term and licences convert to perpetual paid-up. Conditional renewal elements inapplicable. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § XIV Effect of Termination | Wind-down runs one way against us; no Array obligation to assist or to return/export our data, and 14.2 applies only on termination, not expiry. Inserting a reciprocal fallback clause (90 days' assistance; data export within 30 days). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Representations, Warranties and Covenants (15.1–15.4) | Only Effective-Date status/IP representations, plus a full disclaimer in 15.4; conformity deferred to future supply and quality agreements. No warranty, duration or remedy today. Inserting fallback 90-day Materials / 30-day services warranty as new 15.5. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (18.9) | Mutual and largely at fallback, but consent to non-successor assignments is unfettered while Affiliate assignments already carry a reasonableness standard. Adding "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed". No change-of-control exit runs against us. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions | No insurance covenant anywhere despite Array's indemnity and recall exposure. Inserting new 18.15 at fallback (E&O USD 1m; cyber and privacy USD 2m). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They should be presented as must-haves rather than trades:

1. **Mandatory arbitration seated outside the accepted jurisdictions (GOVLAW, § 17.3).** All non-Expert disputes go to binding ICC arbitration seated in Osaka whenever Array demands. We need exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County state and federal courts, with temporary injunctive relief preserved elsewhere. The New York law selection in 18.3 stays as drafted.
2. **Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 8.2).** Our only relief today is if Array itself commercialises a Competing Product. We need the 12-month cap and an automatic exit on Array's failure to meet its Article 9 supply obligations, service levels or delivery dates — drafted to operate whether or not a separate supply agreement is signed.
3. **Post-termination non-compete of undefined length (NONCOMPETE, § 8.2).** The Ono-only tail to an undefined "[ * ] anniversary" must go, with the in-term covenant capped and carve-outs for our internal Development and acquisitions.
4. **No termination for convenience during development and pre-launch (T4C, § 13.2).** The exit does not arise until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products, and the notice figure is redacted and cannot be tested. We need an at-will right at any time on 30 days' notice.
5. **Unlimited audit rights (AUDIT, § 4.9(a)).** Array's open-ended facility entry right has no frequency cap at all; a once-yearly limit and fixed notice are required.

We would also treat **INDEMN** as effectively non-negotiable in substance: the absence of any IP infringement indemnity for the licensed Array Patents, Array Know-How and Array-supplied Products — combined with 11.4 leaving the Subject Party to defend at its own expense and no non-infringement warranty in Article 15 — is not a position we can accept alongside the breadth of our own 16.1 indemnity.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the three unverified findings before anything is tabled.**
   - *IP (critical):* the automated review did not complete. Run a full manual review of ownership of deliverables and Customer Data; we currently have no conclusion on this rule.
   - *LOL-CAP:* confirm the numbering and placement of the new Section 16.7 and, with the deal team, whether the USD 1,000,000 floor is adequate — given consideration is an upfront fee, milestones and royalties, the floor is likely to be the operative figure. Confirm the carve-out language captures all of our payment obligations under Articles 6 and 7.
   - *T4C:* re-verify the 13.2 edit and confirm the pro rata refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments, leaving the non-refundable 6.1 upfront licence fee alone.
2. **Resolve the redacted figures.** Several conclusions turn on "[ * ]" values — the in-term exclusivity period and post-termination anniversary in 8.2, the 13.2 waiting period and notice, the 7.4 underpayment threshold and the Wind-down Period. Ask Array to unredact so we can confirm which items are genuinely off-market.
3. **Sequence the 8.2 edits.** EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE both bite on Section 8.2; we should table a single consolidated redline (12-month cap, supply-failure exit, deletion of the tail, acquisitions carve-out) and conform Array's termination trigger and the Article XIV cross-reference so nothing dangles.
4. **Flag the T4C / 8.2 interaction internally.** Making the at-will exit available immediately means the Competing Product tail could bite earlier; that is a further reason to delete the tail in the same pass.
5. **Table the gap-fillers as standard.** Transition assistance and data return (Article XIV), the 15.5 performance warranty and the 18.15 insurance covenant are all drafted at fallback and should be presented as ordinary course additions.
6. **Diarise a re-test of MINCOMMIT** when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are negotiated — forecasting and binding-order terms could introduce a commitment that does not exist today.
7. **Do not redline** the compliant items (LD, LICENSE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, RENEWAL). In particular, Section 14.3's liquidated damages and the 13.1 perpetual paid-up licence conversion run in our favour and should be protected in any counterparty mark-up."}
